# Rise and Battle the Day
## Scripture
"Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go." – Joshua 1:9
## Reflection
Every morning you wake up, a battle is already waiting. Not against flesh and blood, but against complacency, distraction, and the quiet pull to just coast through another day. Joshua faced the same tension. He was stepping into Moses' shoes, leading a nation, and staring down fortified cities. God's command to him wasn't "try harder" — it was "be strong and courageous." Notice the foundation: *the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.*

Courage isn't the absence of fear; it's obedience in the presence of it. Strength isn't self-made — it's borrowed from the God who never leaves the room. Too many men wait to feel ready before they act. God says act *because* He's with you. That's the difference between a man who drifts and a warrior who advances.

Today, don't wait for motivation. Make your bed, open your Bible, show up at work with integrity, and lead your family with intention. The battle is real, but so is your God. Rise and battle the day — not in your own strength, but in His.
## Daily Challenge
Before your first task today, do 20 pushups and pray: "Lord, make me strong and courageous for Your glory." Then text one brother and ask how you can pray for him.
